newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds rise, peso issues take off.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds rise, peso issues take off.

text.p: Argentine bonds finished mostly higher Friday as recent optimism translated into increased buying of peso-denominated bonds.
"There was strong demand for peso bonds from abroad," said a trader at a large Argentine bank. "There was genuine buying."
The peso-denominated Bocon Proveedor 1 due 2007 outperformed the market, rising 75 centavos to 93.00. The shorter-dated peso Bocon Previsional 3 due 2002 rose 25 centavos to 88.25.
The traditional benchmark in the local market, the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 fell $0.25 to 120.35, while Argentina's FRB due 2005 rose 1/8 to 84-6/8.
The trader added that interest in the "Pre 2" suffered not least because of the decreasing duration of that bond.
Another trader said "with this strength of the peso bonds," there is a "good picture" for the market in the coming week.
When peso bonds outperform, it means the devaluation risk of Argentina falls, indicating improved confidence in assets.

Still, some traders have said the recent compression of the spread between peso and dollar bonds may have gone too far. Indeed, the second trader noted some local pension funds reportedly booked some profits on peso bond this session.

But the overall mood of the market has improved all week, particularly on the increasing hopes that growth is rebounding strongly. The government announced Wednesday third quarter growth rose a larger-than-expected 6.6 percent from the same period a year earlier.
In the money markets, call money rates fell to 6.85 percent from 7.55 percent.
